note: Reviewed lifespans for data/hist-clio.js (Cliopatria). The machine FINDS (scripts/build-hist-clio.mjs: a row drawn more than FINDING_SLACK years outside the lifespan Wikidata states for a QID shown to be that polity) and this file JUDGES. `rows` act on the map: before `s`, from the year after `e`, and inside each `gaps` span [from, to] (astronomical; `s`, `e` and the years outside a gap are inside; `from` and `to` themselves are in the gap — two lives under one name with the years between them belonging to neither) the shape is drawn without the name, and its card says which name Cliopatria gives and the year the historical record (`history`) places the beginning or the end (`circa`: that year is approximate) — the bound is history's, `wd` is the Wikidata item for the polity that states the same or a nearby year. `refuted` are findings examined and NOT applied, with the reason (`why`: date-disputed, other-identity or name-not-claim); a `side` limits one to that side. A finding is judged by name and side; a `gaps` span judges the end side (the item ended where the gap begins, and the name after it is a second life). `pending` are findings not yet judged: they are drawn as Cliopatria states them, and the gate fails on any finding in none of the three lists — so a new one arrives counted. Gate: npm run check:histclio.

rows.name: Byzantine Empire
rows.history: Constantinople fell to the Ottomans on 29 May 1453, ending the Byzantine Empire; the Despotate of the Morea (to 1460) and the Empire of Trebizond (to 1461) were separate successor states.

rows.name: New Netherland
rows.history: England seized New Amsterdam in 1664 and kept it by the Treaty of Breda (1667); the Dutch reconquest of 1673 was handed back by the Treaty of Westminster in 1674.

rows.name: Denmark-Norway
rows.history: The Treaty of Kiel (14 January 1814) ceded Norway to Sweden and ended the union of Denmark and Norway.

rows.name: Golden Horde
rows.history: The Golden Horde's last remnant, the Great Horde, was destroyed by the Crimean Khanate in 1502.

rows.name: Republic of Florence
rows.history: Alessandro de' Medici was made hereditary Duke of the Florentine Republic in 1532, ending the republic; the Grand Duchy of Tuscany followed in 1569.

rows.name: Swedish Empire
rows.history: The Great Northern War ended Sweden's period as a great power; the Treaty of Nystad (1721) ceded the eastern Baltic provinces to Russia.

rows.name: Almohad Caliphate
rows.history: The Marinids took Marrakesh in 1269, ending the Almohad Caliphate.

rows.name: Almoravid Dynasty
rows.history: The Almohads took Marrakesh in 1147, ending Almoravid rule.

rows.name: Caliphate of Córdoba
rows.history: The Caliphate of Córdoba was abolished in 1031 and broke up into the taifa kingdoms.

rows.name: Hamdanid Emirates
rows.history: The Hamdanid emirate of Mosul ended in 979 and the emirate of Aleppo in 1004.

rows.name: Ngô Dynasty
rows.history: The Ngô dynasty ended in 965, followed by the Anarchy of the Twelve Warlords and the Đinh dynasty (968).

rows.name: Serbian Empire
rows.history: The Serbian Empire ended with the death of Stefan Uroš V in 1371; the Serbian Despotate (1402–1459) was a later successor state.

rows.name: Saadi Sultanate
rows.history: The last Saadi sultan was killed in 1659; the Alaouites had taken Morocco by 1668.

rows.name: Astrakhan Khanate
rows.history: Muscovy conquered Astrakhan in 1556 and annexed the khanate.

rows.name: Byeonhan
rows.history: The Byeonhan confederacy developed into the Gaya confederacy during the 3rd and 4th centuries; Silla annexed the last Gaya states in 562.

rows.name: Cao
rows.history: The state of Song conquered the state of Cao in 487 BC.

rows.name: Chen
rows.history: King Hui of Chu annexed the state of Chen in 479 BC.

rows.name: County of Urgell
rows.history: After the revolt of Count James II of Urgell failed in 1413, the county was confiscated and joined to the Crown of Aragon.

rows.name: Duchy of Anhalt
rows.history: The duchies of Anhalt-Dessau, Anhalt-Köthen and Anhalt-Bernburg were separate states until they were united as the Duchy of Anhalt in 1863.

rows.name: Duchy of Thuringia
rows.history: King Dagobert I set Radulf over the Thuringians as duke in 631/632; before that Thuringia was ruled directly by the Franks after the fall of the Thuringian kingdom in 531.

rows.name: Dál Riata
rows.history: Cináed mac Ailpín, king of Dál Riata, became king of the Picts c. 843; the joint kingdom was called Alba by 900.

rows.name: Fifteenth Dynasty of Egypt
rows.history: Ahmose I took Avaris and expelled the Hyksos Fifteenth Dynasty c. 1550 BC, founding the Eighteenth Dynasty.

rows.name: First Hellenic Republic
rows.history: The London Conference of 1832 made Greece a kingdom under Otto of Bavaria, ending the First Hellenic Republic.

rows.name: First Toungoo Empire
rows.history: The First Toungoo Empire collapsed when Pegu fell in 1599; the Restored Toungoo (Nyaungyan) kingdom that followed ruled until 1752.

rows.name: French Indochina
rows.history: The Indochinese Union was created in 1887 from Cochinchina (French from 1862), the protectorates of Annam and Tonkin, and Cambodia.

rows.name: Halych-Volhynia occupation
rows.history: Roman the Great united the principalities of Halych and Volhynia in 1199; before that they were separate principalities of Rus’.

rows.name: Himyarite Kingdom
rows.history: Aksum conquered Himyar in 525; the Aksumite-installed kings Abraha and his sons ruled Yemen until the Sasanian conquest c. 570.

rows.name: Holy Roman Empire
rows.history: Otto I was crowned emperor in Rome in 962; before that his realm was the East Frankish (German) kingdom.

rows.name: Khmer Empire
rows.history: Ayutthaya sacked Angkor in 1431; the court moved south and the post-Angkor Kingdom of Cambodia followed.

rows.name: Khoshut Khanate
rows.history: Güshi Khan of the Khoshut conquered Tibet and founded the Khoshut Khanate in 1642; before that the Khoshut were a tribe of the Oirat confederation.

rows.name: Kingdom of Armenia
rows.history: The Sasanians deposed the last Arsacid king of Armenia, Artaxias IV, in 428 and made the country a marzpanate.

rows.name: Kingdom of Georgia
rows.history: The Kingdom of Georgia broke up in civil war after 1466 and in 1490 was formally divided into the kingdoms of Kartli, Kakheti and Imereti.

rows.name: Kingdom of Italy
rows.history: Charlemagne conquered the Kingdom of the Lombards in 774 and had his son Pepin crowned King of Italy in 781; Cliopatria’s rows of 568–774 are the Lombard kingdom.

rows.name: Kingdom of Seisyllwg
rows.history: Hywel Dda joined Seisyllwg to Dyfed c. 920, forming the kingdom of Deheubarth.

rows.name: Lakhmid Kingdom
rows.history: Khosrow II deposed the last Lakhmid king, al-Nuʿman III, in 602; al-Hira was then governed by Sasanian appointees until the Muslim conquest of 633.

rows.name: Later Zhou
rows.history: The Later Zhou was a Five Dynasties regime of 951–960; Cliopatria’s rows of 750–256 BC are the Eastern Zhou, which ended in 256 BC.

rows.name: Magna Frisia
rows.history: Charles Martel killed the Frisian king Poppo at the Battle of the Boarn in 734, ending the Frisian kingdom; the Frisians east of the Lauwers were subdued by Charlemagne by 785.

rows.name: Maynila
rows.history: Miguel López de Legazpi took Maynila in 1571 and founded Spanish Manila on its site.

rows.name: Middle Kingdom of Egypt
rows.history: Conventions end the Middle Kingdom with the Twelfth Dynasty (c. 1802 BC) or with the Thirteenth (c. 1650 BC), when the Hyksos Fifteenth Dynasty took the north.

rows.name: Natalia Republic
rows.history: Britain annexed the Natalia Republic in 1843 as the Colony of Natal.

rows.name: Novgorod Republic
rows.history: Novgorod expelled Prince Vsevolod Mstislavich in 1136, the conventional beginning of the republic; before that it was a principality of Kievan Rus’.

rows.name: Peloponnesian League
rows.history: After Thebes defeated Sparta at Leuctra (371 BC), Sparta’s allies made a separate peace with Thebes in 366/365 BC and the Peloponnesian League dissolved.

rows.name: Portuguese Ceylon
rows.history: The Dutch took Colombo in 1656 and Jaffna, the last Portuguese stronghold in Ceylon, in 1658.

rows.name: Principality of Vladimir-Suzdal
rows.history: Dmitry Donskoy bequeathed the grand principality of Vladimir to his son in 1389 as a patrimony of Moscow, merging it into Muscovy.

rows.name: Pskov Republic
rows.history: Novgorod recognised Pskov’s independence by the Treaty of Bolotovo in 1348; before that Pskov belonged to the Novgorod Republic.

rows.name: Ptolemaic Kingdom
rows.history: Ptolemy became satrap of Egypt after Alexander’s death in 323 BC and took the royal title in 305 BC; before 323 BC Egypt was part of Alexander’s empire.

rows.name: Roman Kingdom
rows.history: The expulsion of Tarquinius Superbus in 509 BC ended the Roman Kingdom and began the Republic.

rows.name: Seventeenth Dynasty of Egypt
rows.history: The Theban Seventeenth Dynasty ended with Kamose c. 1550 BC; his brother Ahmose I founded the Eighteenth Dynasty.

rows.name: Shang Dynasty
rows.history: The Zhou conquered the Shang at the Battle of Muye, conventionally dated 1046 BC (estimates range from 1122 to 1027 BC).

rows.name: Shunten Dynasty
rows.history: By the traditional chronology of the Ryūkyū histories, the Shunten dynasty ruled 1187–1259 and was followed by the Eiso dynasty (1260–1349).

rows.name: Sultanate of Malacca
rows.history: Portugal took Malacca in 1511; the sultan’s line continued as the Sultanate of Johor.

rows.name: Sur Empire
rows.history: Akbar’s victory at the Second Battle of Panipat in 1556 ended the Sur Empire.

rows.name: Taifa of Algeciras
rows.history: Al-Muʿtadid of Seville annexed the taifa of Algeciras in 1058; no later taifa of Algeciras is recorded.

rows.name: Taifa of Almería
rows.history: The Almoravids took Almería in 1091; it was a taifa again in 1145–1147 until Alfonso VII of Castile took it in 1147, and no later taifa of Almería is recorded.

rows.name: Taifa of Saltés and Huelva
rows.history: Al-Muʿtadid of Seville annexed the taifa of Huelva and Saltés in 1051; no later taifa there is recorded.

rows.name: Upper Burgundy
rows.history: Rudolph II united Upper and Lower Burgundy in 933, forming the Kingdom of Arles.

rows.name: Western Satraps
rows.history: Chandragupta II of the Gupta Empire conquered the Western Satraps, defeating Rudrasimha III, c. 405–415.

rows.name: Xu
rows.history: The state of Wu destroyed the state of Xu in 512 BC.

rows.name: Emirate of Nejd
rows.history: The Second Saudi State (Emirate of Nejd, the QID) fell to the Rashidis of Ha’il at the Battle of Mulayda on 21 January 1891, and Riyadh was ruled from Ha’il until Ibn Saud retook it on 13 January 1902. His Emirate of Riyadh and Nejd (later of Nejd and Hasa, the Sultanate of Nejd from 1921) is the second life Cliopatria draws under the same name to 1925; between 1892 and 1901 no Saudi Emirate of Nejd existed.

rows.name: Empire of Haiti
rows.history: The First Empire of Haiti (the QID) began when Dessalines was proclaimed emperor in 1804 and ended with his assassination on 17 October 1806; the State and Kingdom of Haiti in the north and the Republic in the south followed, unified as a republic in 1820. Soulouque proclaimed the Second Empire on 26 August 1849 and abdicated on 15 January 1859; Haiti was a republic thereafter. Cliopatria draws «Empire of Haiti» from 1805 to 1915 without a break.

refuted.name: Inca Empire
refuted.history: After the Spanish conquest (1533) the Neo-Inca State held Vilcabamba until 1572; Cliopatria's last row (1564–1571) is that state.

refuted.name: Carolingian Empire
refuted.history: Wikidata's item ends at the partition of Verdun (843); Carolingian kings ruled West Francia until 987, which is the realm Cliopatria draws.

refuted.name: Kingdom of Israel
refuted.history: Cliopatria's rows to 722 BC are the northern Kingdom of Israel, destroyed by Assyria in 722 BC; the QID it carries is the united monarchy.

refuted.name: Alodia
refuted.history: The Nubian kingdoms grew out of the collapse of Kush (Meroe) c. 350; Alodia’s founding is undated and it is first attested in the 6th century, so neither year is a stated beginning.

refuted.name: Bidar Sultanate
refuted.history: Qasim Barid ruled Bidar as regent of the Bahmanis from 1492; his son Amir Barid declared independence c. 1527, and the sultanate is dated 1492–1619 in most accounts.

refuted.name: Burgundian Kingdom
refuted.history: The Franks conquered the Kingdom of the Burgundians in 534; Cliopatria’s rows of 602–660 are the Merovingian sub-kingdom of Burgundy, which the record also calls the Kingdom of Burgundy.

refuted.name: Burma
refuted.history: Cliopatria’s 1820–1885 rows are the Konbaung kingdom of Burma, annexed by Britain in 1885; the QID is the modern state founded at independence in 1948.

refuted.name: Caucasian Albania
refuted.history: Albanian kings fought Pompey in 65 BC; the Sasanians abolished the monarchy in 461, restored it under Vachagan III (c. 487) and made Albania a marzpanate c. 510.

refuted.name: Chu
refuted.history: Chu was a Zhou-era state from the 11th century BC whose rulers took the royal title in 704 BC; Wikidata’s year is the start of the Spring and Autumn period.

refuted.name: County of Besalú
refuted.history: Besalú was a Carolingian county under its own counts from the late 9th century; Wikidata’s 988 is when the Catalan counties stopped recognising Frankish suzerainty.

refuted.name: County of Ribagorza
refuted.history: Ribagorza had its own counts from c. 872 under Raymond I.

refuted.name: County of Savoy
refuted.history: The County of Savoy was raised to a duchy by Emperor Sigismund in 1416; Cliopatria names the continuing Savoyard state by its earlier title.

refuted.name: Dauphiné
refuted.history: Cliopatria’s 1260–1349 rows are the independent Dauphiné of Viennois ruled by its dauphins until Humbert II sold it to France in 1349; the QID is the French province that followed.

refuted.name: Eastern Moghulistan
refuted.history: The QID is undivided Moghulistan; after 1514 Chagatayid Moghul khans ruled the Yarkent Khanate and the Turpan khanate in the Tarim basin until the Dzungar conquest of 1680.

refuted.name: Elam
refuted.history: Proto-Elamite Susa and Anshan formed a state society from c. 3200 BC; the first Elamite dynasty (Awan) is dated c. 2700 BC.

refuted.name: Empire of Kanem
refuted.history: Kanem existed from the 8th or 9th century; its Sayfawa ruler Hummay converted to Islam c. 1085.

refuted.name: Funan
refuted.history: Chenla absorbed Funan in the late 6th and early 7th centuries; Chinese records note Funan embassies until the 640s.

refuted.name: Giudicato of Cagliari
refuted.history: The Sardinian judicates emerged from Byzantine rule between the 9th and 11th centuries; Cagliari’s judges are documented from the 11th century.

refuted.name: Gurjara-Pratihara Dynasty
refuted.history: Nagabhata I founded the Pratihara kingdom c. 730 and fought the Arab invasions in the 730s.

refuted.name: Janapada of Aśmaka
refuted.history: The chronology of the mahajanapadas rests on the uncertain dating of the Buddha; no event fixes the end of Assaka.

refuted.name: Janapada of Gandhāra
refuted.history: Cyrus the Great conquered Gandhāra c. 535 BC, and Darius I’s Behistun inscription (c. 518 BC) lists it as a satrapy; Cliopatria’s 500 BC is within that range.

refuted.name: Janapada of Kosala
refuted.history: Magadha under Ajatashatru annexed Kosala in the 5th century BC; the date rests on the uncertain dating of the Buddha.

refuted.name: Kadamba Empire
refuted.history: The Chalukyas reduced the Kadambas of Banavasi to vassals between c. 540 and the 560s.

refuted.name: Karkota Dynasty
refuted.history: Durlabhavardhana founded the Karkota dynasty in the early 7th century; the reign dates derived from Kalhana’s Rājataraṅgiṇī differ by decades.

refuted.name: Khanate of Sibir
refuted.history: The Siberian Khanate grew out of the Khanate of Tyumen (from the 1420s); its seat moved to Qashliq c. 1490.

refuted.name: Kingdom of Bhutan
refuted.history: Bhutan was unified as a state by Zhabdrung Ngawang Namgyal in the 1630s and became a hereditary monarchy in 1907; Cliopatria names the continuing state by its later title.

refuted.name: Kingdom of Brittany
refuted.history: Nominoe ruled Brittany from 831 and won independence at Ballon in 845; his son Erispoe was recognised as king in 851.

refuted.name: Kingdom of Brycheiniog
refuted.history: Brycheiniog had native kings until the Norman conquest by Bernard de Neufmarché in 1088–1093.

refuted.name: Kingdom of Castile
refuted.history: Castile was a county, autonomous under Fernán González from the 930s, and became a kingdom under Ferdinand I (1035/1037) or Sancho II (1065).

refuted.name: Kingdom of Denmark
refuted.history: Gorm the Old ruled a Danish kingdom from Jelling from c. 936; Harald Bluetooth’s Jelling stone (c. 965) claims he won all of Denmark.

refuted.name: Kingdom of Gwent
refuted.history: Gwent was joined to Morgannwg in the mid-10th century but had its own kings again in the 11th, until Caradog ap Gruffydd (died 1081).

refuted.name: Kingdom of Gwynedd
refuted.history: Gwynedd’s princes ruled until the English conquest of 1282–1283 (Statute of Rhuddlan, 1284); 1216 is when Llywelyn ab Iorwerth became overlord of native Wales.

refuted.name: Kingdom of Janggala
refuted.history: Airlangga divided his realm into Janggala and Panjalu (Kediri) c. 1045.

refuted.name: Kingdom of Lazica
refuted.history: Lazica (Egrisi) remained a Byzantine-dependent principality until the Kingdom of Abkhazia absorbed it in the 780s.

refuted.name: Kingdom of Morgannwg
refuted.history: The early kingdoms of south-east Wales (Glywysing, Gwent, Morgannwg) have no recorded founding; the name Morgannwg is traditionally derived from a 7th- or 8th-century king Morgan.

refuted.name: Kingdom of Northumbria
refuted.history: Æthelfrith united Bernicia and Deira c. 604, forming Northumbria.

refuted.name: Kingdom of Poland
refuted.history: The QID is the Kingdom of Poland of 1025–1385; after the Union of Krewo (1385) the Crown of the Kingdom of Poland continued in union with Lithuania.

refuted.name: Kingdom of Poland
refuted.history: Mieszko I’s Piast realm (from c. 960, baptised 966) is the state Cliopatria draws; its rulers were crowned kings in 1025 and 1076.

refuted.name: Kingdom of Serbia
refuted.history: Cliopatria’s 1188–1351 rows are the medieval Serbian state of the Nemanjić (crowned kings from 1217, empire from 1346); the QID is the modern kingdom of 1882.

refuted.name: Kingdom of Sophene
refuted.history: Arsames founded Sophene c. 260 BC and Tigranes the Great annexed it c. 94 BC, but Rome restored Sophene as a client kingdom (Sohaemus, AD 54) until Trajan annexed Armenia in 114.

refuted.name: Kingdom of Urartu
refuted.history: Urartu fell c. 590–585 BC, probably to the Medes; one reading of the Nabonidus Chronicle has Cyrus campaign against it in 547 BC.

refuted.name: Kingdom of the Iberians
refuted.history: Ashot I ruled the Bagratid principality of Iberia (Tao-Klarjeti) from 813; his descendant Adarnase IV took the royal title in 888.

refuted.name: Lavo Kingdom
refuted.history: Lavo (Lopburi) was a Dvaravati-period polity whose founding is undated; local tradition places it in the 7th century.

refuted.name: Makuria
refuted.history: Makuria emerged from the collapse of Kush (Meroe) c. 350; its founding is undated and it is first attested in the 6th century.

refuted.name: Montenegro
refuted.history: Cliopatria’s 1853–1915 rows are the Principality (1852) and Kingdom (1910–1918) of Montenegro; the QID is the state independent since 2006.

refuted.name: Nepal
refuted.history: Prithvi Narayan Shah took Kathmandu in 1768, founding the Kingdom of Nepal; the QID’s 2008 is the federal republic.

refuted.name: Netherlands Antilles
refuted.history: The Dutch colony of Curaçao and Dependencies (from 1815) was renamed the Netherlands Antilles in 1948 and became an autonomous country in 1954; Cliopatria names the continuing colony by its later name.

refuted.name: Nobatia
refuted.history: Nobatia emerged in Lower Nubia after the collapse of Kush (Meroe) c. 350; its founding is undated (King Silko is attested c. 450).

refuted.name: Oirat Confederation
refuted.history: The Oirat league persisted alongside the rising Dzungars until Galdan Boshugtu subdued the other Oirat chiefs in the 1670s and took the title of khan in 1678.

refuted.name: Old Kingdom of Norway
refuted.history: Harald Fairhair’s unification of Norway is dated by the sagas to c. 872, by modern estimates to c. 880–900.

refuted.name: Principality of Capua
refuted.history: Capua was a Lombard gastaldate and county from the 840s with its own rulers, who took the princely title c. 900.

refuted.name: Principality of Jersika
refuted.history: Jersika is first recorded in the early 13th century (Henry of Livonia); its founding is undated.

refuted.name: Principality of Koknese
refuted.history: Koknese is first recorded in the early 13th century (Henry of Livonia); its founding is undated.

refuted.name: Principality of Rostov-Suzdal
refuted.history: Rostov was a Rus’ appanage principality from the early 11th century; under Yuri Dolgorukiy (from c. 1125) it became the independent principality of Rostov-Suzdal.

refuted.name: Principality of Theodoro
refuted.history: The Gothic principality of Theodoro took shape in the 14th century; its first known prince is attested in the 1360s, and its origins are undated.

refuted.name: Qataban
refuted.history: Hadramawt absorbed Qataban in the late 2nd century AD; proposed dates range from c. 150 to c. 200.

refuted.name: Serbian Despots
refuted.history: Prince Lazar’s Moravian Serbia (from 1371) passed to his son Stefan, who took the title of despot in 1402.

refuted.name: Small Horde
refuted.history: The Lesser Nogai Horde, founded in 1557 on the North Caucasus steppe, remained a nominal dependency of the Crimean Khanate; the QID is the Great Nogai Horde, broken by the Kalmyks in the 1630s.

refuted.name: Sultanate of Mempawah
refuted.history: Mempawah was ruled by a Dayak line before the Bugis prince Opu Daeng Menambon became its ruler c. 1740 and made it an Islamic sultanate.

refuted.name: Sultanate of Oman
refuted.history: The Al Said dynasty has ruled Oman (as Muscat and Oman) since 1744; the QID’s 1970 is the renaming to the Sultanate of Oman.

refuted.name: Swiss Confederation
refuted.history: The Old Swiss Confederacy dates from the alliance of 1291; the QID’s 1848 is the federal state.

refuted.name: Tabal Kingdom
refuted.history: Assyrian records name kings of Tabal until the mid-7th century BC (Mugallu under Ashurbanipal).

refuted.name: Taifa of Niebla
refuted.history: Niebla was a taifa again in 1145–1150 and in 1234–1262, when Alfonso X took it; the QID is the first taifa (to 1053).

refuted.name: Taifa of Silves
refuted.history: Silves was a taifa again in 1144–1155; the QID is the first taifa (to 1063).

refuted.name: Taifa of Valencia
refuted.history: Valencia was a taifa again in 1145–1172 and in 1229–1238, when James I took it; the QID is the first taifa (to 1094).

refuted.name: Tarumanagara
refuted.history: Tarumanagara is known from King Purnawarman’s inscriptions of the 5th century; a founding in 358 rests on the late Wangsakerta manuscripts.

refuted.name: Unified Silla
refuted.history: Silla lost most of its territory in the Later Three Kingdoms period (from 892) but survived until its last king surrendered to Goryeo in 935.

refuted.name: Vakataka Kingdom
refuted.history: Vakataka rule ended in the mid-6th century; the last well-attested king, Harishena (c. 475–500), was followed by obscure successors.

refuted.name: Visigothic Kingdom
refuted.history: The Visigoths were settled in Aquitaine as federates in 418, founding the kingdom of Toulouse; Euric ruled independently from c. 475.

refuted.name: Western Moghulistan
refuted.history: The QID is undivided Moghulistan; after 1514 Chagatayid Moghul khans ruled the Yarkent Khanate and the Turpan khanate in the Tarim basin until the Dzungar conquest of 1680.

refuted.name: Western Xia
refuted.history: The Tangut Li clan ruled the Ordos as a de facto independent state from the 980s; Li Yuanhao proclaimed the Western Xia empire in 1038.

refuted.name: Yue
refuted.history: The QID is Minyue (334–110 BC); Cliopatria’s rows are the Spring and Autumn state of Yue, whose king Goujian reigned from 496 BC and which Chu defeated c. 334 BC.

refuted.name: Zhu
refuted.history: Zhu was a Zhou vassal state from the Western Zhou period; Wikidata’s year is not its founding.

refuted.name: Đại Việt
refuted.history: Đại Việt was the name of the Vietnamese state until 1804; the QID is the Mạc dynasty (1527–1677), one of its ruling houses.
